newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Weak grain futures seen prompting Taiwan orders.
newsitem.headline: Weak grain futures seen prompting Taiwan orders.

text.p: Falling U.S. futures prices could prompt Taiwan to place up to four tenders in the week of October 20 for a total of 70,000 tonnes of U.S. corn and up to 200,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans, local traders said on Friday.
Taiwan's Breakfast Soybeans Procurement Association's Taichung division may seek tenders for two 54,000-tonne U.S. soybeans within two weeks, traders said.
The group's Kaohsiung division is also expected to place a tender for a 54,000-tonne shipment of U.S. soybeans, they added.
Both divisions said they expected soybean futures prices to drop to below US$7 per bushel in near term due to peak harvest season.
"The U.S. soybean could drop to test its support between US$6.7 to US$6.8 per bushel before harvest season ends in November," a Formosa Oilseeds executive said by telephone.
Buyers said pressures from U.S. corn harvest season could bring corn prices to below US$2.8 per bushel and test support at US$2.7 per bushel.
"The corn will remain bearish until mid-November when the harvest season ends," a Feed Industry Group buyer said.
Taiwan's FGEP corn buying group is expected to retender within two weeks for its 54,000 tonnes of U.S. corn, traders said.
The FGEP shipment would be slated for delivery from December 10-25 from U.S. Gulf or December 26 to January 9, 1997 from the Pacific Northwest, traders said.

Taiwan's Hui Shung Group is also expected to tender for a combined shipment of 16,000 tonnes of corn and 38,000 tonnes of soybeans, traders said. The Hui Shung Group's shipment would be slated for delivery in March.
